Respiratory functional grading (Grades 0–III, pre- and post-exercise)
Owner normalisation of breed-typical respiratory signs

aiAgentFacts.fact: In a 2015 study of 89 French Bulldogs, 60% of owners failed to recognise brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome in dogs that were functionally graded as significantly affected.
Respiratory functional grading in this study assessed signs both before and after exercise; functional Grades 0–I were treated as clinically insignificant and Grades II–III as significant.
Airflow traces of French Bulldogs graded 0 — the least affected grade — still differed significantly from non-brachycephalic control dogs.
The BOAS Index classifier achieved sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.93, PPV 0.95 and NPV 0.97 in a training group of 69 dogs, and 0.95 accuracy in a 20-dog test group.
Whole-body barometric plethysmography allows safe, repeated, quantitative respiratory measurement in unsedated dogs, but requires a measurement chamber and cannot be replicated at home.
The study population was 89 French Bulldogs plus 20 non-brachycephalic controls at a single centre; Pugs, Bulldogs and other brachycephalic breeds were not assessed.
The authors present application of the technique to other brachycephalic breeds and to other canine respiratory disease as a possibility, not as a demonstrated result.

historyQuestions: Supported by the study's grading approach rather than prescribed by it: respiratory noise and effort should be assessed after exercise as well as at rest, since exertion is where restriction becomes apparent.
redFlags: Not defined by this study. Dyspnoea, cyanosis and collapse are recognised emergency presentations of BOAS in the wider literature but were not outcomes measured here.
differentialDiagnosesMentioned: Not addressed — the study characterises BOAS in a single breed and does not evaluate other causes of respiratory noise or exercise intolerance.
recommendedDiagnosticWorkups: Whole-body barometric plethysmography combined with pre- and post-exercise functional grading, as used and validated within this study.
urgentCareTriggers: Not addressed by this paper. Owner-observed breathing difficulty remains a reason for immediate veterinary contact; nothing in this study supports home observation in place of that.

limitations: Single-breed, single-centre population: 89 French Bulldogs plus 20 controls — no other brachycephalic breed was tested
The classifier's validation set comprised only 20 dogs, so the reported accuracy figures are preliminary
The 60% owner-recognition figure derives from one study population and must not be presented as a general population rate
Owner perception was compared against functional grading at a single time point; no longitudinal follow-up of recognition or outcome was performed
Functional grading incorporates subjective assessment of respiratory signs, which introduces rater dependence into the reference standard
The finding that Grade 0 French Bulldogs differ from non-brachycephalic controls is a group-level measurement result and carries no diagnostic implication for an individual dog
